# Pagination

Marker- and offset-paginated list operations return a paginator — the list
method *is* the paginator. You drive it with `.next().await`, which yields one
element at a time and threads the cursor for you:

```rust
let mut pages = client.folders.list_items(folder_id, None);
while let Some(item) = pages.next().await {
    let item = item?;
    // use item
}
```

The paginator stops when the last page is reached. It owns a copy of the
options you pass, so your value is never mutated.

## Events

`client.events.stream` follows Box's long-poll event stream: `.next().await`
yields the events after `stream_position` (`"now"` when unset), each once — Box
may deliver an event twice — then waits on a real-time server until Box reports
a change. It lists a fresh server when Box asks it to reconnect, and retries a
long poll that times out. A failed call is yielded once and ends the stream;
drop the stream to stop it:

```rust
let mut events = client.events.stream(None);
while let Some(event) = events.next().await {
    let event = event?;
    // use event
}
```

## Representations (PDF, text, thumbnails)

`client.files.get_representation_content` downloads a rendering of a file that
Box generates on demand — a PDF, its extracted text, page images. `rep_hints`
names it as Box's `X-Rep-Hints` header does; `asset_path` picks one asset of a
multi-asset representation (`"1.png"` for a page) and is `""` for a single-file
one. It waits while Box generates the representation, up to `max_wait`
(`runtime::DEFAULT_REPRESENTATION_WAIT` when `None`), and returns an error if Box
fails to:

```rust
let text = client
    .files
    .get_representation_content(file_id, "[extracted_text]", "", None)
    .await?;
```
